title: Controlling the 3D view
text: default, coord_3d() uses perspective projection, objects farther viewer appear smaller. dist parameter controls camera distance center data cube — larger values produce less distortion. Set persp = FALSE switch orthographic projection, parallel lines 3D remain parallel 2D rendering. Orthographic projection equivalent viewing infinite distance can useful technical schematic plots.  Perspective projection enlarges nearby objects shrinks distant objects. graphical objects whose size defined spatial coordinates (like polygon tiles figure ), resizing always happens inherent data projection. properties like line widths point text sizes, separate “depth scaling” process changes sizing apply perspective. can adjust switch latter behavior specifying scale_depth parameter individual geom/stat function (control scaling data layer) coord_3d() (control scaling gridlines, ticks, axis text).
code: (p + coord_3d(yaw = 45, dist = 1.1) + ggtitle("dist = 1.1")) +   (p + coord_3d(yaw = 45, dist = 2) + ggtitle("dist = 2")) +   (p + coord_3d(yaw = 45, persp = FALSE) + ggtitle("persp = FALSE")) +   plot_layout(ncol = 3)

title: Controlling the 3D view
text: Standard ggplot2 themes work ggcube. Adding complete theme behaves expected:  ggcube also adds several theme elements 3D-specific styling. One important category foreground panel elements, control cube faces rendered front data. inherit background counterparts, styling panel.background affects background foreground faces, panel.foreground targets front faces. ggcube’s element_rect() extends ggplot2’s version alpha parameter transparency. particularly useful foreground panels — default panel.foreground uses alpha = 0.2 front faces don’t obscure data:  axis labels, ggcube adds axis.text.z axis.title.z elements inherit axis.text axis.title respectively. default, axis text, ticks, grid lines get sizes/widths scaled apply depth perspective. can controlled coord_3d(scale_depth = ); see documentation details. Axis titles scaled depth. margin argument element_text() controls padding titles, labels, cube edges.  full set 3D-specific theme elements: panel.foreground: Fill border foreground cube faces (inherits panel.background) panel.border.foreground: Border foreground faces (inherits panel.border) panel.grid.foreground: Grid lines foreground faces (inherits panel.grid) panel.grid.major.foreground: Major grid lines foreground faces (inherits panel.grid.foreground) axis.ticks.z: Z-axis tick (inherits axis.ticks) axis.text.z: Z-axis tick labels (inherits axis.text) axis.title.z: Z-axis title (inherits axis.title)

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: essential ingredient ggcube plot coord_3d(). Adding standard ggplot includes z aesthetic creates 3D plot:  standard ggplot2 layers like geom_point() work 3D automatically. ggcube also provides 3D-specific layer functions surfaces, paths, volumes, text, described . ggcube works within ggplot2’s 2D graphics engine, important things understand rendering works. 3D layer projects geometry onto 2D plane, depth sorting determine elements appear front others. sorting happens within layer, across layers — just standard ggplot2, later layers drawn top earlier ones regardless 3D depth. means layer order code matters, complex multi-layer scenes may require thought stacking.
code: ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, z = drv, color = class)) +       geom_point() +       coord_3d()

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: coord_3d() controls 3D scene projected onto 2D. Rotation specified via three angles — pitch (tilt around x-axis), roll (tilt around y-axis), yaw (spin around z-axis):  Alternatively, direction gives direction plot viewed vector: coord_3d(direction = c(1, 1, 1)) looks cube xmax-ymax-zmax corner. direction() helper builds vectors azimuth elevation, views lights. Perspective projection default, making distant objects appear smaller. dist parameter controls strength effect (larger values = less distortion), persp = FALSE switches orthographic projection parallel lines stay parallel. scales parameter controls axis ranges map visual size. "free" (default) stretches axis independently fill cube, "fixed" preserves relative scale data (like coord_fixed() 2D). ratio parameter lets set custom proportions three axes. zoom adjusts overall framing without changing rotation projection. See 3D view article comprehensive guide view parameters.
code: ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, drv, color = class)) +       geom_point() +       coord_3d(pitch = 0, roll = 60, yaw = 0, dist = 1.4,                ratio = c(2, 1, 1), panels = "all") +       theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"),             panel.foreground = element_rect(alpha = .1))

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: standard ggplot2 geoms designed around 2D coordinate assumptions, won’t render correctly coord_3d(). (exception geom_point(), works box shown , albeit ordering sizing limitations.) ggcube provides range 3D-native layer functions cover common 3D plot types, including points, surfaces, bars, paths, text. ’s quick tour main categories.

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: Several geoms stats work together render surfaces. geom_surface_3d() renders data tessellated surface, geom_contour_3d() creates layer-cake contour stacks, geom_ridgeline_3d() shows cross-sectional slices:  Stats like stat_function_3d(), stat_smooth_3d(), stat_density_3d() generate surface data functions, model fits, kernel density estimates. stats can paired surface geoms. See 3D surfaces article detail surface plotting options.
code: ggplot(mountain, aes(x, y, z)) +       geom_surface_3d(aes(fill = z, color = z)) +       scale_fill_viridis_c() + scale_color_viridis_c() +       coord_3d(ratio = c(1.5, 2, 1), expand = FALSE, panels = "zmin") +       light(direction = c(1, 0, 0)) +       guides(fill = guide_colorbar_3d()) +       theme_light()

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: geom_point_3d() extends scatter plots depth-scaled point sizes (closer points shown larger), proper depth sorting (closer points plotted top), optional reference lines points project onto cube faces:
code: ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, z = drv, fill = class)) +       geom_point_3d(size = 3, shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = .1,                     ref_lines = TRUE, ref_faces = c("ymax", "xmax")) +       coord_3d()

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: geom_path_3d() connects observations depth-sorted, depth-scaled line segments:  geom_segment_3d() also available drawing individual segments defined start end coordinates.
code: x <- seq(0, 20*pi, pi/16) spiral <- data.frame(x = x, y = sin(x), z = cos(x), time = 1:length(x)) ggplot(spiral, aes(x, y, z, color = time)) +       geom_path_3d() +       scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue", "purple", "red", "orange")) +       coord_3d() +       theme_light()

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: geom_col_3d() produces 3D column charts, geom_bar_3d() creates 3D histograms automatic binning, geom_voxel_3d() renders arrays cubes:
code: ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +       geom_bar_3d(bins = 20, width = c(.5, 1)) +       coord_3d(scales = "fixed", ratio = c(1, 3, .25), yaw = 60) +       scale_z_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +       theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: geom_hull_3d() computes renders triangulated hulls 3D point clouds, including convex alpha hulls:
code: ggplot(sphere_points, aes(x, y, z)) +       geom_hull_3d(method = "convex", fill = "#9e2602", color = "#5e1600") +       coord_3d()

title: Introduction to ggcube

code: ggplot(iris, aes(y = Sepal.Length, x = Species, fill = Species)) +       stat_distributions_3d() +       scale_z_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, NA))) +       coord_3d() +       theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Introduction to ggcube
text: geom_text_3d() renders text 3D, either “billboard” labels always face camera, polygon outlines can oriented direction:
code: df <- expand.grid(x = c("H", "B"), y = c("a", "o", "u"), z = c("g", "t")) df$label <- paste0(df$x, df$y, df$z) ggplot(df, aes(x, y, z, label = label, fill = x)) +       geom_text_3d(method = "polygon", facing = "zmax",                    size = 5, weight = "bold") +       coord_3d(scales = "fixed", light = NULL)

title: Lighting and shading
text: Lighting can set two levels: Plot-level: adding light(...) plot applies layers. can appear anywhere plot expression, coord_3d(). (Lighting can also passed coord_3d(light = ...), useful want reusable coord object carries lighting; supplying places error.) Layer-level: geom_*_3d(light = light(...)) overrides plot-level setting layer. Use light("none") disable lighting entirely, light = NULL layer inherit plot-level setting (default layer behavior). add second layer plot, override inherited light settings disable lighting layer:  fill color parameters control aesthetics get modified lighting. default TRUE:  Lighting works solid aesthetically-mapped colors:
code: p + geom_hull_3d(aes(x = x + 2.5), fill = "#9e2602", color = "#5e1600",                  light = "none") (p + ggtitle("fill + color (default)")) +   (p + light(fill = TRUE, color = FALSE) + ggtitle("fill only")) ggplot(sphere_points, aes(x, y, z)) +   geom_hull_3d(aes(fill = x, color = x)) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   scale_color_viridis_c() +   guides(fill = guide_colorbar_3d()) +   coord_3d() +   light("direct")

title: Lighting and shading
text: method parameter controls lighting model: "diffuse" (default): Soft, atmospheric lighting. surfaces pointing directly away light source fully dark. "direct": Hard lighting. surfaces angled beyond 90 degrees light fully dark. "rgb": Maps surface orientation RGB color space, replacing base colors entirely. "none": Disables lighting across plot, except layers declare .
code: (p + light(method = "diffuse") + ggtitle('"diffuse" (default)')) +   (p + light(method = "direct") + ggtitle('"direct"')) +   (p + light(method = "rgb") + ggtitle('"rgb"')) +   plot_layout(ncol = 3)

title: Lighting and shading
text: mode parameter controls lighting modifies colors. applies "diffuse" "direct" methods ("rgb"). two color modes: "hsv" (default): Modifies value component HSV color. Highlights preserve hue; shadows fade black. "hsl": Modifies lightness component HSL color. Highlights fade white; shadows fade black. two modes give identical results grayscale base colors.

title: Lighting and shading

title: Lighting and shading
text: direction parameter length-3 vector specifying light comes ; example, direction = c(0, -1, 0) lights plot negative y direction. anchor parameter controls whether direction relative data axes camera: anchor = "scene" (default): Direction relative data axes rotates plot. direction = c(1, 0, 0) always lights surfaces facing “xmax” face. anchor = "camera": Direction fixed relative viewing pane. direction = c(1, 0, 0) always lights surfaces facing right side plot, regardless rotation.  Directions can also given angles direction(), takes azimuth (compass bearing, measured clockwise positive y axis) elevation (degrees xy plane). often easier want raise lower light without changing side comes . light comes negative x side (azimuth 270), low high:  Printing light shows direction ways, can help translating two: compare light directions side side, move light around interactively, see light_azimuth light_elevation arguments orbit_3d() animate_3d(), view facets facet_wrap_views() facet_grid_views(), covered animation multiple views article.

title: 3D Plotting with ggplot2
text: ggcube lets build 3D figures using ggplot2. Use create 3D surfaces, volumes, scatter plots, complex layered visualizations using familiar ggplot2 syntax aes(x, y, z) coord_3d(). package provides variety 3D-specific geoms render surfaces, prisms, points, paths, text 3D; also works standard ggplot2 layer functions. can control plot geometry 3D projection parameters, apply range 3D lighting models, mix 3D layers 2D layers rendered cube faces. Standard ggplot2 features like faceting, themes, scales, legends work expected. 3D plots wonderful exploration, storytelling, data art. note precise quantitative communication, occlusion perspective distortion can problematic, 2D usually better choice.

Example: terrain surface using geom_surface_3d():  Example: terrain surface using geom_contour_3d():  Example: mathematical surface using geom_function_3d():  Example: fitted model surface using geom_smooth_3d():
code: ggplot(mountain, aes(x, y, z)) +       geom_surface_3d(aes(fill = z, color = z)) +       scale_fill_viridis_c() + scale_color_viridis_c() +       coord_3d(ratio = c(1.5, 2, 1), expand = FALSE, panels = "zmin",                light = light(direction = c(1, 0, 0))) +       guides(fill = guide_colorbar_3d()) +       theme_light() ggplot(mountain, aes(x, y, z)) +       geom_contour_3d(fill = "black", color = "white", linewidth = .5) +       coord_3d(yaw = 60, ratio = c(1.5, 2, 1), light = "none") +       theme_void() ggplot() +       geom_function_3d(fun = function(x1, x2) cos(x1) * sin(x2),                        xlim = c(-pi, pi), ylim = c(-2*pi, 2*pi),                        fill = "#7a2100", color = "#b3725b",                         grid = "right1", linewidth = .2) +       coord_3d(yaw = 160, roll = -70,                 scales = "fixed", ratio = c(1, 1, 2)) +       labs(x = expression(x[1]),            y = expression(x[2]),            z = expression(cos(x[1]) %*% sin(x[2]))) +       theme_minimal() # Generate scattered 3D data set.seed(123) d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(50),                 y = rnorm(50)) d$z <- d$x + d$x^2 - d$y^2 + rnorm(50)  # Plot GAM fit with uncertainty layers ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z)) +        geom_smooth_3d(aes(fill = after_stat(level)),                      method = "gam", formula = z ~ te(x, y),                      se = TRUE, level = 0.99,                      color = "black", grid = "equilateral") +       scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "darkorchid4", "steelblue")) +       coord_3d(light = NULL)

text: major limitation 3D figures can’t get full view data single angle. One way mitigate rotating figure view data different directions. ggcube offers animated rotation via animate_3d(), interactive drag--rotate plots via orbit_3d(). See animation interaction article details. ’s example rotating gif:

NULL (default), lighting left plot specifies. move plot-level light set light() coord_3d(light = ), must directional (position-based); error use lighting disabled layer light. light's anchor respected: default anchor = "scene" light moves around data, animating yaw light_azimuth together partly cancels ; anchor = "camera" moves around viewer. nframes, fps, duration Control animation length speed. Specify two three; third computed duration = nframes / fps. Defaults: nframes = 100, fps = 10. width, height Dimensions animation pixels. Defaults 480 x 480. res Resolution ppi rendered frames. Default 96. Controls size point-based text/lines/point elements relative plot. See ?grDevices::png details. renderer renderer function combines image frames animation file.
